newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia July-March budget deficit A$9.163 bln.
newsitem.headline: Australia July-March budget deficit A$9.163 bln.

text.p: Australia's underlying budget deficit for the nine months to March, the first nine months of fiscal 1996/97, was A$9.163 billion, compared with A$13.266 billion a year earlier, Finance Minister John Fahey said on Wednesday.
The headline balance -- which includes asset sales -- was a A$5.170 billion deficit, compared with a A$8.322 billion deficit for the same period last fiscal year, Fahey said in a statement.
Government finances are highly seasonal and cannot be extrapolated to estimate a final outcome for the fiscal year to June 30, 1997.
Revenue growth to March was 8.4 percent, compared with estimates in the government's mid-year budget review of 5.8 percent.
Outlays grew 4.3 percent, compared with mid-year budget review projections of 3.8 percent, Fahey said.
Revenue growth was fuelled by an 8.4 percent increase in tax receipts over the same period in 1995/96.
The main increases in spending were in social security and welfare, and lower state government debt repayments.
The monthly headline balance for March was a A$2.834 billion surplus, compared with a surplus of A$722 million a year earlier.
The underlying balance for the month was a A$2.793 billion surplus, compared with a A$777 million surplus in March 1996.
